messages.author: 8c68636401b6ddd4
messages.subject: Intercept formulas
parts:
Hi all,

I have a small question about fixing intercepts:

If "x~ 1" means that the intercept for x is set to 1, what does "x ~ 0*1" then mean?

Thanks for your help!

Best,
Annaleena

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Intercept formulas
parts:
Annaleena

x~1 doesnt mean that the intercept is set to 1, operator is both pieces "~1", so it indicates that intercept parameter without any fixe values. When you add x~0*1, you are fixing the intercept to 0
